---
title: "Model building"
---

## Define a biological model

Start from the system of interest: what state the model carries, how it changes,
which context influences an update, and what observations it produces.
`cellerator.modeling.Model` accepts caller-defined dynamics and observation
functions; `Cell` associates a persistent identity with model-native state and
an independent time. `StepContext` carries time, step size, inputs, parameters,
random source, and metadata. `StepResult` carries updated state and optional
events/effects. State is opaque to this interface.

Then add the representation and computational mechanisms appropriate to the
model. Cellerator supports model-native structures, sparse relations, events,
continuous numerical changes, stochastic updates, learned components, and
compositions. Choose Torch modules where their parameter ownership and
autograd help. Use Cellerator native operations and layouts where modeled
identity, geometry, or dependency structure changes useful computation.

The existing Torch module surface is intentionally small. `Product2Module` is a real
`torch.nn.Module` with trainable coefficients, persistent indices, native
preparation, and first-order gradients. The optional CUDA `MechanismModule`
owns a specific native indexed-mechanism handle and lifecycle. Sparse support
modules model explicit ranked-gene and event-slice consumers. These components
have distinct backend, data, and maturity boundaries; they are not a uniform
layer stack. See [operations](operations.qmd) and the
[Python binding guide](development/python-bindings.md) for details.

## Keep scientific meaning with the model owner

Cellerator should expose reusable contracts without assigning biological
meaning to an input by convention. A scientific consumer defines how an entity,
relation, feature, event, or state is interpreted and validates that
interpretation. A numerical API should state the accepted identities, ordering,
value types, update behavior, and derivative contract without silently
inventing a domain ontology. The broader Cellerator framework can still provide
natural modeling objects: `Cell` denotes a persistent model instance, while
the model defines the meaning of its state, behavior, and observation.

The AnnData adapter makes matrix selection explicit and preserves cell/feature
identities and sparse values. It does not select a layer, normalize, infer
events, or create biological meaning without the caller's instruction.
Established preprocessing remains upstream in AnnData, Scanpy, or
RAPIDS-singlecell.

## Parameters, state, and structure

Treat model structure, current activity, state values, and learned parameters
as separate things. A parameter update should not rebuild immutable structure
when an operation permits reuse, and a change of activity should have an
explicit support or invalidation path. A layout reorder must preserve the
mapping back to logical entities, outputs, and gradients. See
[layout and execution](layout_execution.qmd).

Shared parameters belong to reusable model components; evolving private state
belongs to each cell instance. Relations describe possible interactions,
activity gates decide which are relevant now, and physical layout maps logical
identity into an execution representation. Cellerator's data structures may
be sparse, ragged, relational, event-based, tensor backed, or custom. Choose
`torch.nn.Module` when it usefully owns learned parameters, buffers, or
composition; a callable dynamics rule or native API can express other work.

## Execution fields are experimental

The current `ExecutionField` composes a prepared Product2 module and makes
structure rebinding explicit. It is experimental, CPU FP32, and has no JIT or
live recompilation. Ordinary model use does not depend on an execution field.
The [experimental fields note](development/experimental-fields.md) documents
its exact boundary.
